about.title: Pinole Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, often at grocery stores, apartment stairwells, or business entrances near San Pablo Avenue or the I-80 corridor in Pinole. What matters afterward is what the property owner knew about the hazard and whether they had a fair chance to fix it or warn people. That's the heart of a California premises liability claim: proving notice. Wet floors, broken pavement, poor lighting in a parking structure, or a loose handrail can all become the basis of a claim if the owner was careless about a known risk. Because evidence like surveillance footage and incident reports can disappear quickly, acting soon after a fall matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself — we simply connect injured Pinole residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, gather the right records, and explain your options under Contra Costa County practice, all without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Pinole Fall

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California law generally requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help identify evidence — like prior complaints or maintenance logs — that supports this.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Pinole businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Both Ways
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery can be reduced by your share of fault but isn't necessarily barred. An attorney can help present the facts fairly, especially if the property owner's insurer tries to shift blame onto you.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Pinole?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the fall to file a claim, though it can be shorter if a government entity — like the City of Pinole or Contra Costa County — owns the property. Missing these deadlines can end your case, so it's worth talking to an attorney early. LawProactive can help connect you with someone who can confirm the timeline for your specific situation.

items.question: What if the fall happened at a business near San Pablo Avenue or I-80?
items.answer: The location doesn't change the core legal question: did the property owner or manager know about the hazard and fail to fix or warn about it? Businesses along busy corridors often have more foot traffic, which can actually make hazard awareness easier to establish if there were prior complaints or incidents. An independent attorney can help gather that kind of evidence.

items.question: Do I need to prove the store or landlord was careless?
items.answer: Yes, in most cases you need to show the owner had actual or constructive notice of the dangerous condition and didn't act reasonably to fix it or warn visitors. This is different from simply proving a hazard existed. An attorney can help evaluate whether the facts of your fall meet this standard under California law.
